official_documentation.title: AMD RDNA3 Instruction Set Architecture, sections3.4.2,7.9 and instruction S_ROUND_MODE
official_documentation.claims: The mode register exposes four scalar round settings. WMMA floating types support nearest-even only. The isolated gfx1151 run verifies unchanged WMMA outputs across those settings while actual scalar additions distinguish directed modes.

conclusions: The native diagnostic completes with state controls, guards, immutable inputs and compiler-intrinsic parity passing. It does not qualify raw WMMA as exact integer arithmetic:1183848 of4194304 mode/dtype/permutation comparisons contain fractional errors, with repeated inputs clearly counted.

The two-term original-input example(-221*-29)+(87*-68) has exact integer sum493 but native bits1140228088 decode to492.999755859375. Both BF16 and FP16 expose the same example, and the full per-family failure counts agree across types and modes. This isolates mixed-sign arithmetic without a model, prepared core conversion or long carry chain.

The all-nonnegative and all-negative-product families have no observed mismatches. Mixed-sign K2/K4/K8/K16 and exact-cancellation families fail. These finite families do not prove a universal positive-product contract or a general error formula.

Nearest-integer conversion repairs every observed small-integer output, but remains a diagnostic calculation only. No rounding repair, tighter envelope, product route or release qualification follows from this finite sample. Changing ordinary wave round mode does not provide canonical SM121 semantics on this device.

Host compilation uses address/undefined sanitizers and strict warnings; encoded BF16/FP16 operands and every permuted dot are checked against an independently computed int64 result. The existing54 Rust/427 Python(two skips), C/ABI and clippy checks are comparable because only this standalone diagnostic source changes.
